Notice of Delisting or Failure to Satisfy a Continued Listing Rule or Standard; Transfer of Listing. On September 21, 2026, Netcapital Inc. (the “Company”) received a letter (the “Notice”) from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) notifying the Company that, because the Company has not yet filed its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended July 31, 2026 (the “Form 10-Q”), and remains delinquent in filing its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2026 (the “Form 10-K”), the Company does not comply with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1), which requires listed companies to timely file all required periodic financial reports with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”). As previously disclosed in the Company’s Current Report on Form 8-K filed on August 27, 2026, the Company received a letter from Nasdaq on August 24, 2026 relating to its failure to timely file the Form 10-K. Pursuant to that letter, the Company has until October 23, 2026 to submit to Nasdaq a plan to regain compliance with respect to both the Form 10-K and the Form 10-Q. If Nasdaq accepts the Company’s plan, Nasdaq may grant the Company an exception of up to 180 calendar days from the due date of the Form 10-K, or until February 9, 2027, to regain compliance. If Nasdaq does not accept the Company’s plan, the Company will have the opportunity to appeal that determination to a Nasdaq Hearings Panel. The Notice has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company’s common stock, which will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “NCPL,” subject to the Company’s continued compliance with Nasdaq’s other continued listing requirements. The Company intends to submit a plan to regain compliance to Nasdaq within the required timeframe and intends to file the Form 10-K and the Form 10-Q as soon as practicable. However, there can be no assurance that Nasdaq will accept the Company’s plan, that the Company will be able to regain compliance within any exception period granted by Nasdaq, or that the Company will otherwise maintain compliance with Nasdaq’s continued listing requirements. On September 25, 2026, the Company issued a press release announcing its receipt of the Notice, as required by Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(b). A copy of the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated herein by reference. Forward-Looking Statements This Current Report on Form 8-K contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, including statements regarding the Company’s intention to submit a plan to regain compliance with Nasdaq’s listing rules, the timing of the filing of the Form 10-K and the Form 10-Q, and the Company’s ability to maintain the listing of its common stock on Nasdaq. These statements are based on management’s current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially, including the Company’s ability to complete the required audit and review of its financial statements, the availability of financing, Nasdaq’s acceptance of the Company’s plan, and the other risks described in the Company’s filings with the SEC. The Company undertakes no obligation to update any forward-looking statement, except as required by law. Item 9.01. Financial Statements and Exhibits. (d) Exhibits. Notice of Delisting or Failure to Satisfy a Continued Listing Rule or Standard; Transfer of Listing. As previously disclosed, on February 4, 2026, Netcapital Inc. (the “Company”) received a letter from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) notifying the Company that the closing bid price of its common stock had been below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days, and that the Company therefore did not comply with the minimum bid price requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). On October 7, 2026, the Company received a letter from Nasdaq notifying the Company that, for the 10 consecutive business days from September 23, 2026 through October 6, 2026, the closing bid price of the Company’s common stock had been at $1.00 per share or greater. Accordingly, Nasdaq determined that the Company has regained compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), and the matter is now closed. As previously disclosed, the Company remains out of compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) as a result of its failure to timely file its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2026 and its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended July 31, 2026. The Company has until October 23, 2026 to submit to Nasdaq a plan to regain compliance with that rule. The October 7, 2026 letter does not address or affect that matter, and there can be no assurance that Nasdaq will accept the Company’s plan or that the Company will regain compliance with Rule 5250(c)(1). On October 13, 2026, the Company issued a press release announcing that it has regained compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) and the engagement of Adeptus as its independent registered public accounting firm. A copy of the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated herein by reference. Forward-Looking Statements This Current Report on Form 8-K contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, including statements regarding the Company’s plan to regain compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) and its ability to maintain the listing of its common stock on Nasdaq. These statements are based on management’s current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially, including the Company’s ability to maintain a closing bid price of at least $1.00 per share, its ability to complete the required audits and reviews of its financial statements, the availability of financing, Nasdaq’s acceptance of the Company’s compliance plan, and the other risks described in the Company’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The Company undertakes no obligation to update any forward-looking statement, except as required by law. Item 4.01. Changes in Registrant’s Certifying Accountant. On October 8, 2026, the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company approved the engagement of Adeptus Partners, LLC (“Adeptus”) as the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm, succeeding Fruci & Associates II, PLLC (“Fruci”), whose resignation effective August 12, 2026 was previously reported in the Company’s Current Report on Form 8-K filed on August 18, 2026 (the “August 8-K”). Adeptus has been engaged to audit the Company’s consolidated financial statements as of and for each of the fiscal years ended April 30, 2022 through April 30, 2026, including the opening balance sheet as of April 30, 2021, and to review the Company’s unaudited interim financial information for each of the quarters in the fiscal year ended April 30, 2026. As previously disclosed in Item 4.02 of the August 8-K, the Company’s previously issued audited financial statements for the fiscal years ended April 30, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025, and the related unaudited interim financial statements identified in the August 8-K, should no longer be relied upon. Adeptus’s engagement to re-audit those fiscal years is intended to support the Company’s evaluation and completion of any required restatement and the filing of its delinquent periodic reports. The Company has not completed its evaluation of the corrections that may be required, and investors should continue not to rely on those previously issued financial statements. Item 9.01. On October 14, 2026, Netcapital Inc. (the “Company”) closed the first tranche of the transactions contemplated by a Securities Purchase Agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”), dated as of October 13, 2026, with Hinterland Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Hinterland”). Pursuant to the Purchase Agreement, the Company issued to Hinterland a promissory note dated October 13, 2026 in the aggregate principal amount of up to $641,936.66, for an aggregate purchase price of up to $577,743.00, reflecting an original issue discount of up to $64,193.66 (the “Note”), to be funded in up to two tranches. At the closing of the first tranche, Hinterland paid a purchase price of $402,743.00, and the outstanding principal amount of the Note became $447,492.22 (the “First Tranche”). If, within 90 calendar days after the date of the Purchase Agreement, (i) no event of default (or event that with the passage of time would be an event of default) has occurred under the Note, (ii) the Company has not breached the transaction documents, (iii) the Company’s common stock remains listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market, and (iv) the Company becomes current in its reporting obligations under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, including by filing its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2026 and its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended July 31, 2026 (the “Delinquent Filings”), Hinterland is required to fund a second tranche with a purchase price of $175,000.00 (the “Second Tranche”) within five business days after satisfaction of such conditions. Upon the closing of the Second Tranche, the principal amount of the Note will increase by $194,444.44 and accrued interest will increase by $23,333.33. The Note bears a one-time interest charge of 12% on the principal amount of each tranche (up to $77,032.39 in the aggregate), of which $53,699.06 is attributable to the First Tranche. Each tranche matures 12 months after the date on which such tranche is funded. The Note is secured by a pledge of 3,209,685 shares of Class A common stock of KingsCrowd, Inc. held by the Company, pursuant to a Pledge Agreement, dated as of October 13, 2026, among the Company, Hinterland and KingsCrowd, Inc. (the “Pledge Agreement”). Upon an event of default under the Note, in addition to its other remedies, Hinterland will be entitled to exercise the voting rights with respect to the pledged shares and will have a continuing option to transfer ownership of up to all of the pledged shares to itself, in which case the outstanding balance of the Note will be reduced by $0.18 for each pledged share transferred. At any time on or prior to the 180th calendar day after the funding date of each tranche, the Company has a one-time right, upon five trading days’ prior written notice, to prepay such tranche by paying 99% of the outstanding principal amount and 100% of the accrued and unpaid interest of such tranche, plus $750.00 for administrative fees. Hinterland may convert all or any portion of such amount during the notice period. If the Company or any of its subsidiaries receives cash proceeds from any source while the Note is outstanding, including from customer payments, equity or debt issuances or asset sales, the Company must notify Hinterland or publicly disclose such receipt within one business day, and Hinterland may require the Company to apply up to 30% of such proceeds to repay the Note. Amounts not paid when due bear default interest at the lesser of 18% per annum and the maximum amount permitted by law. The Note is convertible at Hinterland’s option at any time on or after the issue date into shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.001 per share (“Common Stock”). Hinterland may deduct $1,950.00 from the conversion amount of each conversion to cover its fees. The conversion price is 85% of the lowest traded price of the Common Stock on the principal market during the seven trading days immediately preceding the applicable conversion date, subject to adjustment. If the conversion price would be less than the par value of the Common Stock, Hinterland may elect to convert at par value with a corresponding increase to the conversion amount. The conversion price is also subject to reduction, at Hinterland’s option, to the effective price of any subsequent issuance of Common Stock or Common Stock equivalents at a lower price, subject to limited exceptions. The Note contains a 4.99% beneficial ownership limitation. The Company is required to reserve for issuance upon conversion of the Note the greater of 5,000,000 shares of Common Stock and four times the number of shares issuable upon full conversion of the Note at the then-applicable conversion price. As additional consideration for each tranche, the Company is required to issue to Hinterland, on the funding date of such tranche, a number of shares of Common Stock (the “Commitment Shares”) equal to 20% of the principal amount of such tranche divided by the closing price of the Common Stock on the trading day immediately preceding such funding date. In connection with the First Tranche, the Company issued 64,387 Commitment Shares to Hinterland. If the issuance of Commitment Shares for any tranche would cause Hinterland’s beneficial ownership to exceed the 4.99% beneficial ownership limitation, the Company will instead issue to Hinterland a common stock purchase warrant to purchase an equal number of shares of Common Stock at an initial exercise price of $0.01 per share (the “Warrants,” and together with the Note, the Commitment Shares, the shares issuable upon conversion of the Note and the shares issuable upon exercise of the Warrants, the “Securities”). Under the Purchase Agreement, the aggregate number of shares of Common Stock that may be issued to Hinterland under the transaction documents is limited to 1,603,685 shares (the “Exchange Cap”) unless shareholder approval is obtained in accordance with Nasdaq Rule 5635(d), subject to adjustment. The Purchase Agreement requires the Company to hold a special meeting of shareholders on or before the date that is 180 calendar days after the date of the Purchase Agreement for the purpose of obtaining such shareholder approval. The Purchase Agreement provides that the Company will use the proceeds for business development and general working capital, subject to specified restrictions. The Purchase Agreement and the Note contain customary and transaction-specific covenants, including transfer agent instructions, legal counsel opinion provisions, public information covenants (including cash payments equal to 3% of the purchase price for public information failures, subject to an exception for the Delinquent Filings if filed within 90 calendar days after the date of the Purchase Agreement), piggy-back registration rights, a right of participation in subsequent financings and a prohibition on variable rate transactions, in each case for the later of 18 months after the date of the Purchase Agreement and the date the Note is extinguished, a most favored nation provision, a requirement to purchase directors’ and officers’ insurance within 60 calendar days after closing, and restrictions on capital stock distributions, stock repurchases and debt repayments, asset sales, affiliate loans, Section 3(a)(9) and 3(a)(10) transactions, and merchant cash advance and similar transactions. The Note contains events of default including, without limitation, payment defaults, failure to deliver conversion shares or maintain the required share reserve, breach of covenants, breach of representations and warranties, receivership, judgments in excess of $100,000, bankruptcy or insolvency events, failure to comply with Exchange Act reporting requirements at any time after February 9, 2027, liquidation, cessation of operations, failure to maintain material assets, restatement of financial statements, transfer-agent-related defaults, cross-default, consummation of a variable rate or prohibited transaction, transmission of material non-public information not cured by a same-day Form 8-K, unavailability of Rule 144 beginning six months after the issue date, trading suspension, halt or delisting, and failure to maintain a market capitalization of at least $3,000,000. Upon an event of default, the Note becomes immediately due and payable in an amount equal to the then-outstanding principal amount plus accrued interest, including default interest, multiplied by 150%, plus costs of collection. Hinterland may, in its sole discretion, convert all or any portion of the Note, including the default amount, into Common Stock pursuant to the terms of the Note. The foregoing descriptions of the Purchase Agreement, the Note, the Warrants and the Pledge Agreement do not purport to be complete and are qualified in their entirety by reference to the full text of the Purchase Agreement, the Note, the form of Warrant and the Pledge Agreement, which are filed as exhibits to this Current Report on Form 8-K and incorporated herein by reference. Item 2.03 Creation of a Direct Financial Obligation or an Obligation under an Off-Balance Sheet Arrangement of a Registrant. The information set forth in Item 1.01 of this Current Report on Form 8-K is incorporated herein by reference. Item 3.02 Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities. The information set forth in Item 1.01 of this Current Report on Form 8-K is incorporated herein by reference. The Securities were offered and sold in a private placement in reliance upon the exemption from registration provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Rule 506(b) promulgated thereunder. Hinterland represented that it is an accredited investor and acquired the Securities for investment purposes. The Company did not use general solicitation or general advertising in connection with the offering. Enclave Capital LLC acted as placement agent in connection with the transaction, and $17,500 was withheld from the purchase price to cover fees owed by the Company to the placement agent. (the “Company”) is filing this Amendment No. 1 on Form 8-K/A (this “Amendment”) to correct Item 4.01 of its Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on October 14, 2026 (the “Original Report”). In the Original Report, the Company said that the Audit Committee of its Board of Directors had approved the engagement of Adeptus Partners, LLC (“Adeptus”) as the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm. Except as stated in this Amendment, it does not amend or update any other information in the Original Report, including Item 3.01 and Exhibit 99.1, and it should be read together with the Original Report and the Company’s other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Item 4.01. Changes in Registrant’s Certifying Accountant. The disclosure under Item 4.01 of the Original Report is corrected and restated in its entirety as follows: On October 8, 2026, the Audit Committee approved the proposed engagement of Adeptus as the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm, to succeed Fruci & Associates II, PLLC (“Fruci”). Fruci’s resignation, effective August 12, 2026, was previously reported in the Company’s Current Report on Form 8-K filed on August 18, 2026 (the “August 8-K”). The proposed engagement was to cover audits of the Company’s consolidated financial statements as of and for each of the fiscal years ended April 30, 2022 through April 30, 2026, including the opening balance sheet as of April 30, 2021, and reviews of the Company’s unaudited interim financial information for each quarter of the fiscal year ended April 30, 2026. The Company prepared the Original Report based on an engagement prepared by and executed with its then-employed Adeptus partner. The Original Report stated that Adeptus had been engaged. Subsequent to the Original Report, Adeptus notified the Company that the engagement had not been completed within the internal structure of Adeptus by the then-employed, now-former partner. Adeptus did not begin any audit or review work for the Company. Accordingly, Adeptus will not serve as, the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm. Adeptus has verbal refused to honor its contract and complete the process to become the Company’s certifying accountant, and Adeptus did not resign or decline to stand for re-election as, and was not dismissed as, the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm. Adeptus did not issue any report on the Company’s financial statements. Fruci remains the Company’s most recent former independent registered public accounting firm for purposes of Item 304(a), and the disclosures about Fruci were provided in the August 8-K. The Audit Committee has begun a search for a successor independent registered public accounting firm. The Company will report the engagement of a successor firm as required by Item 4.01 of Form 8-K. As previously disclosed in Item 4.02 of the August 8-K, the Company’s previously issued audited financial statements for the fiscal years ended April 30, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025, and the related unaudited interim financial statements identified in the August 8-K, should no longer be relied upon. Investors should continue not to rely on those financial statements. The need to engage a successor firm could delay the completion of the re-audits, any required restatement, and the filing of the Company’s Annual Report. Form 20-F ☒ Form 40-F ☐ On October 6, 2026, POMDOCTOR LIMITED (the “Company”) received a staff determination letter (the “Letter”) from the Listing Qualifications Department (the “Staff”) of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) notifying the Company that the bid price of the Company’s American depositary shares (the “ADSs”) had closed below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days, from August 24, 2026 through October 5, 2026. Accordingly, the Company is not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) (the “Minimum Bid Price Requirement”). Ordinarily, a Nasdaq-listed company would be afforded a 180-calendar-day compliance period to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Price Requirement. However, pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iv), a company is not eligible for such a compliance period if it has effected a reverse stock split during the prior one-year period. Because the Company effected a 1-for-18 reverse stock split on June 22, 2026, within the prior one-year period, the Company is not eligible for a compliance period and the Staff issued the delisting determination. As a result, the Staff determined to delist the Company’s securities from The Nasdaq Global Market. Unless the Company timely requests a hearing before a Nasdaq Hearings Panel (the “Panel”) to appeal the Staff’s determination, the Company’s securities will be suspended from trading at the opening of business on October 15, 2026, and Nasdaq will file a Form 25-NSE with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to remove the Company’s securities from listing and registration on Nasdaq. The Company intends to timely request a hearing before the Panel to appeal the Staff’s determination and to present its plan to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Price Requirement. The deadline for the Company to request a hearing is October 13, 2026. A timely hearing request will stay the suspension of the Company’s securities and the filing of the Form 25-NSE pending the Panel’s decision. Accordingly, the suspension of the Company’s securities and the filing of the Form 25-NSE will be stayed while the appeal remains pending. The Company is evaluating the alternatives available to it to regain compliance with Nasdaq’s continued listing requirements. However, there can be no assurance that the Panel will grant the Company an extension of time to regain compliance, that the Company will regain or maintain compliance with the Minimum Bid Price Requirement or any other Nasdaq continued listing requirement, or that the Company’s appeal will be successful. On October 9, 2026, the Company issued a press release regarding its receipt of the Letter. A copy of the press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to this Report on Form 6-K. The information contained in this Report on Form 6-K, including Exhibit 99.1, shall not be deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), or otherwise subject to the liabilities of that section, nor shall it be deemed incorporated by reference into any filing of the Company under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or the Exchange Act, except as expressly set forth by specific reference in such filing. Form 20-F ☒ Form 40-F ☐ Receipt of Nasdaq Notifications Regarding Continued Listing Requirements On October 28, 2026, POMDOCTOR LIMITED (the “Company”) received two letters (the “Letters”) from the Listing Qualifications Department (the “Staff”) of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) regarding deficiencies with respect to certain continued listing requirements of The Nasdaq Global Market. The first Letter notified the Company that, based upon the Company’s MVLS for the 30 consecutive business days from September 16, 2026 through October 27, 2026, the Company no longer meets the requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(b)(2)(A) to maintain market value of listed securities (“MVLS”) of at least $50 million (the “MVLS Requirement”). Pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(C), the Company has a compliance period of 180 calendar days, or until April 26, 2027, to regain compliance with the MVLS Requirement. If at any time during the compliance period the Company’s MVLS closes at $50 million or more for a minimum of ten consecutive business days, Nasdaq will provide the Company with written confirmation of compliance and the matter will be closed. The second Letter notified the Company that, based upon the Company’s MVPHS for the 30 consecutive business days from September 16, 2026 through October 27, 2026, the Company no longer meets the requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(b)(2&3)(C) to maintain a minimum market value of publicly held shares (“MVPHS”) of $15 million (the “MVPHS Requirement”). Pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(D), the Company has a compliance period of 180 calendar days, or until April 26, 2027, to regain compliance with the MVPHS Requirement. If at any time during the compliance period the Company’s MVPHS closes at $15 million or more for a minimum of ten consecutive business days, Nasdaq will provide the Company with written confirmation of compliance and the matter will be closed. If the Company does not regain compliance prior to the expiration of the applicable compliance period, the Company will receive written notification that its securities are subject to delisting. At that time, the Company may appeal the delisting determination to a Hearings Panel. The Company intends to monitor its MVLS and MVPHS and evaluate available options to regain compliance with the applicable continued listing requirements within the compliance period. There can be no assurance that the Company will regain compliance with the applicable Nasdaq continued listing requirements within the compliance period or otherwise maintain compliance with Nasdaq’s other continued listing requirements.
